sovereign_country.strategic_role: 最高信誉财富保护、私人银行合规与楚格州加密谷Web3枢纽

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Automated Dropshipping Networks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–China Free Trade Agreement (signed 2013, in force 1 July 2014)
Switzerland–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1986, as amended)
EFTA Convention (internal free trade framework with EU member states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0), Art. 4–6a and Art. 8; Swiss Code of Obligations (CO, SR 220), Art. 620–644 and Art. 697j–697n; Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons (SR 221.416); FINMA Circular 2011/01 on money laundering.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts) executed public deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary (Notar / Notaire) in the canton of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Swiss instrument; no apostille required for internal registration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each beneficial owner and director-UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or consular section of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Swiss consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Extract from Commercial Register of the incorporating corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Swiss consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of deposit of minimum share capital on a blocked account (Sperrkonto / Consignation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss regulated bank (e.g., UBS, Credit Suisse, canton bank) or Swiss branch of a foreign bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank-letter confirmation; signature verification by Swiss notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Swiss SECO Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and PEP registries. Enhanced due diligence applies where a PEP, PEP family member, or a high-risk jurisdiction is identified. Results and underlying documentation must be retained for at least 10 years under Art. 8 AMLA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX – Zentraler Firmenindex (www.zefix.ch), operated by the Swiss Federal Office for the Register of Commerce and cantonal commercial register offices
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian) or in a foreign language if not misleading; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The legal form suffix must appear in the chosen official language, e.g., 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a formal name rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the cantonal commercial register authority (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce). If the cantonal authority rejects the appeal, the applicant may further appeal to the Cantonal Administrative Court, and ultimately to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne. All appeals must be submitted in the official language of the canton and accompanied by the original rejection notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Pure virtual office without a physical Swiss address and without service acceptance is not permissible for an Aktiengesellschaft. Domiciliation through a licensed trust company or business centre is accepted if the office is physically present in Switzerland, accepts service of legal documents, and the company maintains adequate substance, books, and records at or near this address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10%–15% annual risk; a substance inspection may be triggered if the company is using domiciliation services and generates online retail revenue without significant local activity. This risk increases if the company becomes a payment institution or holds a financial intermediary licence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and trademark conflict screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: In-house legal counsel and/or registered trademark agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per searched name

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial drafting and execution of deed of incorporation (public deed)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal official tariff for deed drafting and notarial act
Cantonal statutory fee schedule (based on incorporated capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Blocked bank account confirmation for minimum share capital (Sperrkonto)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss authorised bank (UBS, Credit Suisse, cantonal bank, etc.)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee schedule, account blocking and confirmation letter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO due diligence file compilation, beneficial owner identification, and PEP/sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss legal counsel and/or compliance provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, hourly fee based on complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, consular legalization, translation and authentication of foreign corporate/personal documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin-country notaries, apostille authorities, and Swiss consular section
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular and notarial tariffs, plus external translation costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Part Five: Commercial Register and Commercial Companies, Articles 620-763 governing the stock corporation (Aktiengesellschaft); in particular Article 626 (mandatory content of the Articles of Association), Article 630 (commercial register application), Article 630a (director eligibility declarations), Article 631 (paid-up capital requirement), Article 640 (audit opt-out), and Article 950 (commercial register information system); supplemented by the Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HregV).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office, operating under the supervisory authority of the Federal Office of Justice; electronic filing via the e-GR / PrivaSphere portal and the Zefix national business name index.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised constitutive incorporation instrument (Gruendungsurkunde / acte constitutif) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten), filed as the statutory registration deed with the Commercial Register and subsequently published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard AG profile requires a minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 (Article 621 OR); at least 20 per cent of the nominal amount, with a hard floor of CHF 50,000, must be paid up in cash before registration; the paid-up portion must be deposited in a blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) at a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank and confirmed by a written bank capital confirmation; contributions in kind require a licensed auditor confirmation; the unpaid balance is callable by the Board of Directors at any time.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED unanimously by the founding board of CH_AG on [date]: 1) The CHF 100,000 authorised share capital, divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 nominal value each, is fully subscribed and taken over by the founders in accordance with the subscription list annexed hereto. 2) The registered office is hereby adopted at [address, canton], and the domiciliation agreement is approved. 3) The following officers are appointed: [Name], Chairman; [Name], Secretary; [Name], Compliance Officer. 4) Daily management is delegated to the Chief Executive Officer. 5) All lawful filings, commercial register entries, and tax registrations are ratified, and the Board is authorised to execute the statutory incorporation steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preliminary company name availability and eligibility check via Zefix
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zefix - Central Business Name Index, operated by the Federal Office of Justice under the Federal Act on Commercial Register Information
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run an electronic availability and structure search on the Zefix portal; verify that the proposed corporate name, which must include the legal form suffix AG, is not identical or confusingly similar to existing trade names or protected marks; download the search record and keep it in the notary file; where a higher degree of certainty is desired, obtain a formal preliminary name certificate from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: Proposed name variants
Brief description of the corporate purpose under ISIC 4791 automated dropshipping
Zefix search output
Shareholder list supporting the name decision record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflicting identical or deceptively similar name is identified, the applicant selects the next available variant and reruns the search; a formal opposition by a prior trademark holder must be resolved by written consent or by adopting a sufficiently distinct name before the notarial step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of the Articles of Association and constitutive deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal notary public (Notariat) in the canton of the registered office, e.g., Notariat of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association (Statuten) with the mandatory content under Article 626 OR: corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose including automated dropshipping and internet retail, nominal share capital of CHF 100,000, share denomination and type, transfer restrictions if any, composition of the Board of Directors, and the audit opt-out resolution; all founders appear before the cantonal notary in person or by notarially certified power of attorney; the notary verifies identity and legal capacity, reads the deed, and records the signatures, thereby issuing the public constitutive instrument.
required_dossiers: Final draft Articles of Association
Valid passport or national identity card of each founder
Zefix name search record
Domiciliation agreement providing the registered office address and the owner's consent
Notarially certified power of attorney for any represented founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies in the notarial deed are cured by a corrective notarial instrument (Berichtigungsurkunde) executed before the same notary; if the purpose clause or capital clause is legally objectionable, the founders re-execute the deed in amended form and the corrected text is appended to the registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of the minimum paid-up capital into a FINMA-licensed blocked capital account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or securities firm authorised to operate statutory blocked capital accounts (Sperrkonto)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account in the name of CH_AG while the company is still in formation; transfer at least CHF 50,000 in freely available funds from the shareholders' private accounts with a clear payment purpose reference; comply with the enhanced KYC and beneficial ownership process applicable under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act given the Medium-Risk_Enhanced commercial classification and the Stripe and PayPal payment rails; obtain the bank's statutory capital confirmation letter (Kapitalbestaetigung) which must state the amount credited and confirm that the funds are irrevocably at the company's disposal; the bank releases the funds only after presentation of the final commercial register extract.
required_dossiers: Notarial constitutive deed and Articles of Association
Passports of all shareholders and directors
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration
Source of funds documentation and personal bank statements
AML/KYC questionnaires including projected payment flows through Stripe and PayPal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises a compliance query, supplement the KYC file with definitive source-of-wealth evidence; if the bank ultimately declines the business relationship, open the account at an alternate FINMA-licensed bank and obtain a fresh capital confirmation; the registration file is ineffective without a written bank confirmation of the paid-up amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory registration application to the Cantonal Commercial Register with SOGC publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered canton, via notary e-submission or the e-GR / PrivaSphere electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application no later than three months after the date of the notarial deed; submit the complete electronic dossier comprising the notarised deed, Articles of Association, bank capital confirmation, sworn declarations of the Board members and the managing director confirming absence of disqualifying insolvency proceedings and criminal convictions, written consent of the owner of the registered office premises, and the name check record; pay the registry and publication fees; the Commercial Register Office conducts the statutory legality review; upon approval, the company acquires legal personality and the incorporation is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Notarised constitutive deed and Articles of Association
Bank capital confirmation (Kapitalbestaetigung)
Director eligibility declarations under Article 630a OR
Written consent of the registered office property owner
Zefix name search record
Fee payment voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register Office issues a deficiency notice (Maengelruege), cure the identified formalities within the stated deadline, generally up to 30 days, by supplying the missing deed, consent, or confirmation; if the defect affects the substance of the incorporation, a notarial corrective resolution is required; failure to respond causes the application to lapse and requires a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Automatic UID number issuance and verification in the federal register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Statistical Office (Bundesamt fuer Statistik) together with the UID registry operated by the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon entry in the Commercial Register, the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) is automatically assigned by the federal administration without a separate application; verify the UID record online at the official uid.admin.ch portal; use the UID on all invoices, customs declarations, VAT returns, and official correspondence; if requested, retrieve the automatically generated statistical enterprise number from the same record.
required_dossiers: Final commercial register extract
Company identification sheet as generated online
Identity of the authorised representative performing the online verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID is not visible online within 15 working days after the commercial register entry, contact the UID Service Desk with the commercial register extract; incorrect master data is remedied by a formal correction recorded through the commercial register file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT registration with the Federal Tax Administration for Swiss distance-selling and dropshipping turnover
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA), VAT Division, through the e-services portal Swing and Form 754
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Swiss VAT if worldwide taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed CHF 100,000 within a 12-month period, which is the standard threshold for automated dropshipping with deliveries into Switzerland; submit the registration no later than 30 days after the threshold is exceeded; provide the UID, estimated turnover, nature of supplies, delivery origins, and the target payment processing platforms (Stripe and PayPal); elect the quarterly return procedure with the standard Swiss VAT rate of 8.1 per cent; where goods are imported into Switzerland, coordinate import VAT settlement with the Federal Customs Administration through the authorised customs declaration procedure.
required_dossiers: UID certificate
Commercial register extract
12-month turnover projection for the first fiscal year
Description of the automated dropshipping supply chain and delivery origins
List of payment service providers and merchant account details for Stripe and PayPal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is late or omitted, file the declaration of liability retroactively and settle the assessed VAT together with default interest; voluntary disclosure before an inspection normally excludes criminal prosecution; if the ESTV questions the registration particulars, a formal statement of rectification may be submitted within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social insurance and compulsory accident insurance employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse), e.g., Ausgleichskasse Zug, together with SUVA or a licensed private accident insurer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after hiring the first employee, including a salaried managing director, register as an employer with the competent Ausgleichskasse and obtain the AHV employer number; register all employees for AHV/IV/EO social insurance; conclude compulsory occupational accident insurance in accordance with the UVG; where the automated dropshipping company operates with no employees, verify whether the statutory officer cover applies and register the compensated officers with the compensation office; maintain wage declarations for the quarterly AHV settlement.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract
Articles of Association
Employment contracts or board compensation scheme
Identity documents of all employees
Accident insurance confirmation from SUVA or a licensed private insurer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Overdue employer registration is cured by retroactive filing and payment of due contributions plus interest; penalties are waived or reduced upon voluntary disclosure before an inspection; if the compensation office disputes the wage base, submit corrected wage statements and documentary evidence of remuneration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal tax registration and opening of the corporate income tax and capital tax file
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Steueramt) of the registered canton, with supplementary federal withholding tax registration at the ESTV for future dividend payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the cantonal company tax number promptly after receipt of the commercial register extract; file the Articles of Association and the opening balance sheet for the first tax assessment; register the company for corporate income tax and capital tax (Kapitalsteuer); if dividend distributions are planned, register for federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer of 35 per cent) and remit the tax upon payment of distributions; agree the cantonal tax calendar and prepare annual statutory accounts in accordance with the accounting provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract
Articles of Association
UID certificate
Opening balance sheet together with the bank capital confirmation
Bank account details and proof of registered office
Director information for tax correspondence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A delayed cantonal tax file is cured by retroactive registration and filing of the relevant declarations; administrative late-filing penalties may be waived upon first-time self-correcting conduct; any contested tax assessment may be challenged through the statutory appeal procedure within 30 days of service.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure automated dropshipping operation under ISIC 4791. No industrial licence or manufacturing authority is engaged. If the company later introduces Swiss-based warehousing or fulfilment activities, the Cantonal Office of Economy and Labour (Amt fuer Wirtschaft und Arbeit) and the municipal trade authority may impose warehouse and logistics operating conditions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required. Swiss law does not issue a specific operating licence for distance selling or automated dropshipping; the commercial register entry constitutes the only statutory authorisation to operate as a retailer. No manufacturing or operational permit is applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU / FOEN), acting through the Cantonal Environment Agency of the registered office canton, e.g., Amt fuer Umwelt des Kantons Zug
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. Automated dropshipping involves no physical manufacturing, no emissions-intensive installation, and no infrastructure project; the activity therefore does not meet the threshold criteria of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV), and no EIA report or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable in the absence of any installation. Should the company subsequently operate a Swiss warehouse or logistics facility, the Federal Waste Ordinance (VVEA), the Packaging Ordinance (VVS), and the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ORRChem) would govern packaging waste, returned goods, and any battery or electronics disposal obligations; no process wastewater or VOC emission thresholds are engaged.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must maintain a valid building fire insurance confirmation (Gebaeudeversicherung); if racking or storage systems are introduced, a structural load certificate and fire safety inspection by the cantonal fire protection authority (Feuerpolizei) under VKF / NVK rules are required. For occupational safety, SUVA and SECO labour-law clearance apply: the company must complete a risk assessment under the Swiss Accident Prevention Ordinance, provide first-aid equipment, conclude mandatory accident insurance for employees, and keep documented workplace instructions in the corporate file.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV; French: Administration fédérale des contributions, AFC), official portal https://www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration and filing via SuisseTax e-portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities entering Swiss VAT nexus must obtain a Swiss VAT number (MWST-Nr./UID CHE) from ESTV via the SuisseTax registration portal or Form 9.2 before commencing taxable supplies. Non-Swiss-established businesses apply directly; Swiss branches and Aktiengesellschaften obtain the business identification number through the Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zefix) after commercial register entry, which imports automatically to ESTV.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss VAT group election per Art. 53 Swiss VAT Act for related enterprises; no check-the-box classification for Swiss AGs; hybrid mismatch rules apply under the Swiss implementation of BEPS Action 2 but there is no unilateral entity classification election; limited cantonal tax consolidation options exist for income tax without changing the federal entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Swiss Value Added Tax; Mehrwertsteuer / Impôt fédéral sur les prestations)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual turnover from taxable supplies for Swiss-established businesses; non-established foreign suppliers have no CHF threshold and must register when performing taxable supplies in Switzerland, subject to distance-selling provisions for imported goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping or mandatory digital fiscal invoice regime. Tax invoices may be issued electronically in any agreed format, but must satisfy statutory VAT invoice content requirements; Swiss standardized e-invoicing formats (eBill/QR-bill) are accepted. ESTV retains full audit rights over electronic records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to outright exports of goods where ownership is transferred to a foreign buyer and goods are physically delivered or transported out of Switzerland, evidenced by a customs declaration. Certain services named in Art. 23 para. 2 Swiss VAT Act and ancillary services directly related to exported goods qualify for zero-rating. Dropshipping transactions qualify only if title passes to the foreign or end customer and the goods are demonstrably exported from Switzerland.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Narwa or Tradenet declaration in Switzerland or official border customs office release),
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / consignment transport documents proving exit from Switzerland,
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/FX receipt proving consideration received from abroad within the documentary evidence record,
Commercial invoice and export purchase orders,
Proof of foreign destination and recipient, including end-customer delivery addresses.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV audits zero-rated exports strictly; if the export proof is missing or incomplete, VAT is retroactively assessed at the standard rate of 8.1%, plus default interest. Proven fraudulent zero-rating triggers criminal tax evasion penalties of up to three times the tax evaded, in addition to reassessed tax and interest, under Art. 106 ff. Swiss VAT Act, with no limitation shield for intentional misdeclaration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank (Banque nationale suisse)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full, unrestricted convertibility of the Swiss franc (CHF) on both current and capital account transactions, in full compliance with IMF Article VIII. There is no foreign-exchange control statute, no central bank approval requirement for cross-border payments, and no restriction on profit distribution, dividend remittance, or repatriation of invested capital. The only binding obligations are (i) FINMA anti-money-laundering identification and reporting duties under the AMLA and (ii) statistical reporting thresholds applicable to financial intermediaries. Profit remittance by an AG requires a formal shareholders' resolution, confirmation of distributable profit per Art. 660 and Art. 671 of the Swiss Code of Obligations (CO), and a 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) at source unless distributions constitute repayment of paid-in capital; no exchange-control approval is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or repatriation timeline exists under Swiss law. Mandatory conversion ratios are zero: export receipts in foreign currency may be retained indefinitely in domestic or foreign bank accounts without any SNB or FINMA mandate. The only relevant duties are commercial bookkeeping and tax reporting obligations (Art. 957 ff. CO; Art. 58 VAT Act), including mandatory balance-sheet recognition of foreign-currency receivables and valuation of open positions per Swiss GAAP (FER) or IFRS; VAT treatment follows Art. 23 VAT Act and does not require FX conversion at customs.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational and Multi-Currency Settlement Account (CHF/USD/EUR), Merchant Collection Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with SIC, SEPA and SWIFT connectivity
Operational Account and Trade Settlement Account
Wealth and Investment Account (not suited for high-volume transaction flows)
Legacy Operational Account (migration backlog; new onboarding discouraged)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, subject to material legal constraints. A foreign e-money institution (EMI) such as Wise, Payoneer, or Revolut may be used only as an auxiliary settlement channel and cannot substitute for a FINMA-supervised bank account. The Banking Act (Art. 1) and FinIA (Art. 5) reserve the taking of deposits from the public to licensed institutions; an offshore EMI soliciting Swiss corporate clients without FINMA authorization is legally fragile. Practical blockers include absence of a Swiss CHF IBAN, no access to SIC instant clearing, non-recognition for Swiss withholding-tax collection accounts, and supplier refusal to accept EMI payouts. Viable model: maintain a Swiss tier-1 bank account as the treasury anchor and statutory settlement account, add a Swiss-regulated fintech (e.g., Swissquote Bank Ltd, Yuh, or Neon) for low-cost payment routing, and deploy the foreign EMI only for niche cross-border payouts where the foreign entity documentation is accepted.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Art. 10 AMLO-FINMA and FINMA Circular 2016/07, the beneficial owners of a corporate client must be identified with reliable documentary evidence. Tier-1 Swiss banks uniformly require: (i) certified true copies of the articles of association (Statuten), a current Handelsregisterauszug (commercial register excerpt), and confirmation of registered office; and (ii) a mandatory compliance interview with at least one authorized signatory or the ultimate beneficial owner. FINMA-compliant video identification is accepted for natural persons under Circular 2016/07, but for the legal entity most banks retain a physical-meeting requirement for first-time onboarding, particularly where the director is non-resident. Remote opening is available at a minority of banks (e.g., ZKB and UBS digital onboarding channels for Swiss-resident signatories); non-resident directors should budget 10–15 business days and a personal branch visit, or use a licensed Swiss fiduciary to coordinate a notarized power-of-attorney and an in-person executive session at the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model flagged as high-volume, low-ticket automated dropshipping with card-based settlement via Stripe and PayPal, resembling transaction-laundering or layering indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (i) executed supplier agreements and marketplace seller-portal screenshots; (ii) order-level reconciliation report covering the first 90 days of operations; (iii) PSP service agreements and settlement statements from Stripe/PayPal evidencing genuine commercial flows; (iv) domain ownership certificates, SSL/TLS configuration, and fulfillment/warehouse logistics contracts; (v) a formal business plan containing unit economics, expected gross margin, chargeback provisioning, and a payment-flow diagram; and (vi) board minutes approving the automated dropshipping model and the designated AML compliance contact.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Atypical sourcing concentration in non-OECD jurisdictions (notably China, Hong Kong SAR, and Turkiye) with elevated counterparty risk and documentary opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) a complete supplier due-diligence file including business registration, beneficial ownership, and bank account details in the supplier's legal name; (ii) signed master supply agreements specifying Incoterms (typically FCA or EXW) and payment terms; (iii) shipping-lane evidence, customs documentation, and tracking reports proving physical goods movement; (iv) a written explanation of import/customs handling (supplier DDP vs buyer direct import); and (v) a risk matrix showing that no supplier is a sanctioned entity and that payment routing avoids OFAC/DEA-listed banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-flow asymmetry: customer receipts arrive via third-party PSPs ahead of supplier payments, creating short-term unverified float and potential misinterpretation as proceeds of unrelated third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) PSP merchant agreements showing settlement cycles (T+1/T+2) and reserve policies; (ii) a pro-forma working-capital model quantifying gross margin, float needs, and chargeback provisioning; (iii) monthly reconciliation statements linking PSP payouts to bank inflows; (iv) confirmations from payment processors regarding the merchant category code and compliance with card network rules; and (v) audited or accountant-reviewed first-quarter financial statements demonstrating that inflows match ordinary e-commerce sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated AG with no credit history and a foreign beneficial owner resident in a higher-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (i) passport copies and proof of residence (utility bill or tax residence certificate); (ii) source-of-wealth documentation (tax returns, asset statements, employment records, or capital-gains evidence); (iii) apostilled power of attorney and board resolutions; (iv) bank confirmation of paid-up share capital per Art. 632 CO; and (v) a professional reference letter from a Swiss-licensed fiduciary or audit firm confirming the client's identity and commercial credibility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered purpose in the commercial register is too broad or too narrow and does not transparently reflect automated dropshipping activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) an updated Handelsregisterauszug with the purpose clause amended to read 'development and operation of e-commerce platforms, including automated dropshipping, and the purchase and sale of goods through remote sales channels' (Art. 626 CO); (ii) board minutes resolving the actual business scope; and (iii) a letter from the registered fiduciary confirming the amendment and confirming that the statutory books and records correspond to the filed purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing options: (i) Share capital increase via notarial deed and commercial register filing, with funds wired by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own account using the purpose specification 'Einlage Kapitalerhoehung / contribution to share capital', plus a bank confirmation (Geldeinzahlungsbestaetigung) per Art. 632/633 CO; (ii) Shareholder loan documented by an interest-bearing loan agreement, wired via MT103 with purpose 'shareholder loan facility', subject to the arm's-length and thin-capitalization safe harbor in Art. 65 VSB 19 (1:1 debt-to-equity as a general rule for non-banks); (iii) Current-account credit (contocorrente) facility with the parent or principal shareholder. Switzerland imposes no purpose-code approval regime; however, the receiving Swiss bank records the SWIFT purpose tag and will require source-of-funds evidence for flows of CHF 100,000 or more. Tax consideration: a 1% Swiss issuance stamp duty (Emissionsabgabe) applies to paid-in capital injections above CHF 1 million, but a shareholder loan structure avoids issuance duty entirely. For inbound transfers from a non-EU shareholder, no notarial reporting to the SNB is required; only the standard client-identification file must be maintained under AMLO-FINMA.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for USD, EUR, and CNY supplier settlements via UBS/ZKB correspondent banking connectivity (direct CHIPS, Fedwire, and TARGET2 access); (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EU suppliers, executed same-day with purpose code 'Goods purchase / Warenkauf'; (iii) domestic SIC and instant-payment rails for CHF disbursements to Swiss suppliers; (iv) commercial documentary letters of credit (MT700) and documentary collections (DP/DA) for large-value or repetitive supplier orders, available but rarely used in card-driven dropshipping; (v) bank-issued virtual corporate cards routed over Visa/Mastercard networks for marketplace payments; and (vi) PSP mass-payout API rails (Stripe Connect, PayPal Payouts) for automated vendor disbursements in EUR, GBP, and USD. Treasury policy recommendation: maintain a minimum 15% operating float in each settlement currency, use SWIFT gpi for end-to-end tracking and same-day exception resolution, and require dual-authorization controls for any outbound wire above CHF 50,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright OTC FX forwards (USDCHF, EURCHF, GBPCHF) under an ISDA 2002 or Swiss Master Agreement for Financial Products (CHF Master Agreement), with ISDA CSD/credit-support annex; no exchange-control permit required.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic currency exposures (e.g., CNY/EUR, TRY/USD, PLN/USD) where deliverable forwards are unavailable in the local market; executable via UBS or ZKB market-making desks.
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) converting USD/EUR receivables into CHF debt-service cash flows, documented under ISDA 2002 with a Swiss Annex and standard credit-support annex.
Exchange-traded FX futures on CME or Eurex (CHF/USD, EUR/CHF contracts) for shorter-dated hedge tenors where margin efficiency is preferred.

FX options and zero-cost collars (vanilla puts/calls, knock-in/knock-out structures) permitted under FinIA, provided the AG qualifies as a professional or institutional client under FinIA Art. 4 or adopts a board-approved hedging policy.

Natural hedging via multi-currency current accounts (Waehrungskontokorrent), including balance-sheet netting of EUR/USD receivables against supplier payables, minimizing actual FX conversion and reducing bid-offer frictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Adoption of annual financial statements and profit appropriation at the Annual General Meeting; minutes retained and annexed to the annual tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting (internal corporate organ); no filing to a state agency at this stage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date (Art. 699 para. 2 OR); for a 31 December year-end the AGM must be held by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors' civil liability for non-compliance; dividend distributions become legally unavailable; continued failure to organize may trigger court dissolution under Art. 731a/731b OR and deletion from the Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal and federal corporate income tax return including adopted financial statements, capital tax schedule and liquidity schedule; annual federal withholding tax reconciliation if no distributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deadline fixed by the canton, normally 6 to 8 months after fiscal year-end (generally 30 June to 30 September for 31 December balance sheets); extension obtainable on reasoned application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% p.a., late-filing surcharge, estimated assessment by the tax office, administrative fine of up to one-third of evaded tax, criminal proceedings for tax evasion, and enforceable tax debt leading to bankruptcy and eventual Commercial Register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT (MWST) return for each VAT filing period (quarterly, semi-annual or annual where FTA-approved)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Value Added Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after expiry of the VAT accounting period; annual accounting period only if granted by FTA (available to small taxpayers whose VAT liability is low)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 5% p.a., administrative penalty of up to three times the amount of tax evaded, summary criminal fines, withdrawal of annual or simplified settlement, and forced collection proceedings that can end in bankruptcy and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Verrechnungssteuer (withholding tax) declaration and payment on any distributions (dividends, constructive dividends, interest) during the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Withholding Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due within 30 days after the end of the calendar month in which the taxable benefit was paid; annual reconciliation return due within 60 days after the tax period, normally by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, fine of up to three times the tax withheld, personal liability of directors and authorised signatories; non-payment can provoke seizure and bankruptcy and subsequent deletion of the entity from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer social security declaration: annual AHV/ALV/EO wage statement and annual occupational pension (BVG) report when the AG employs any staff (including managing director on salary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse) and the occupational pension foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage statement within 3 months after the calendar year-end (31 March); monthly/quarterly advance contributions by the 10th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest on arrears, procedural fines, and statutory lien on employer assets; the compensation fund may initiate debt enforcement leading to bankruptcy and ultimate deregistration of the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full ordinary statutory audit is mandatory if the AG exceeds two of the three thresholds in two consecutive fiscal years: total assets above CHF 20 million, annual net turnover above CHF 40 million, or an annual average of more than 250 full-time employees; listed companies and public-debt issuers are always subject to ordinary audit. Non-threshold AGs must at minimum undergo a limited statutory review unless all shareholders unanimously approve an opt-out, which is allowed only when the company does not employ more than 10 full-time equivalents on an annual average.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements are prepared under the accounting provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963a OR), materially aligned with Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS may be applied voluntarily or mandatorily for consolidated listed groups; tax books follow the duly approved statutory annual accounts on a going-concern accrual basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law imposes no annual UBO confirmation filing. The share register (Aktienbuch) must be updated on each transfer and before voting rights are exercised; any person acquiring 25% or more of a non-listed AG's share capital must be identified as a beneficial owner and entered in the company's register of beneficial owners, with report to the Commercial Register under the 2023 disclosure rules. Bearer shares have been eliminated; all shares of non-listed companies must be registered shares. Changes to directors or auditors must also be reported to the Commercial Register promptly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (with addresses and nationalities)
Minute Book (board and shareholders' meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 2,000 - 10,000 for external domiciliation, registered office and fiduciary/company secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 - 12,000 for an opting-out or limited statutory review engagement; 15,000 - 60,000 for an ordinary statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal (aggregate Swiss effective rate 11.9%–21.0% with cantonal/communal tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box relief (up to 90% income exemption); Notional Interest Deduction (NID); participation exemption on dividends and capital gains (95% exemption); holding company privileged status

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal/Cantonal Corporate Tax Return (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales) filed via eTax / E-Déclaration / WINtax portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after closure of the fiscal year (calendar-year taxpayer: 30 June of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit per annual statutory accounts before corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide taxable income of the Swiss AG, including dropshipping margin booked in Switzerland; exclude foreign PE business income where a DTA exempts it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, open and hidden reserves, retained earnings used for capital tax assessments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare fully paid-in capital (minimum CHF 100,000) and aggregate reserves; verify ownership to support dividend withholding.

loss_carryforward_and_adjustments.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses and deduct tax-exempt income such as participation relief or patent box income.
loss_carryforward_and_adjustments.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate every intercompany charge under the arm's-length principle; retain contemporaneous documentation for offsetting deductions.

box_4.entry_description: Merit carried-forward losses from prior years (within 7-year statutory window).
box_4.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses confirmed in prior assessments are deductible; a change-in-ownership with absorbent tax motive disqualifies loss utilisation.

box_5.entry_description: Swiss federal anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) withheld on Swiss dividend and bond interest income.
box_5.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident AG claims a full refund/credit against corporate income tax by attaching original withholding documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of worldwide dropshipping revenue in corporate returns or creation of fictitious intercompany invoices to shift profit outside Switzerland.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_sanction: Tax fraud fine up to CHF 250,000 plus evaded taxes; non-fraud wilful omission penalised up to 30% of evaded tax (DBG Art. 174, 175).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers and de facto shareholders are co-liable for fines and unpaid civil tax restitution; travel bans and imprisonment up to 3 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.triggering_act: Swiss AG used purely as letter-box company without local employees, business premises, or management decision-making, solely to claim treaty benefits or favourable tax residency.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under Art. 22 VStG; retroactive tax recharacterisation; administrative fines up to CHF 20,000 and adjustments of hidden profit distributions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for damage to creditors under Art. 754 CO; travel restrictions in cooperative tax investigations; possible director disqualification for up to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.triggering_act: Use of automated dropshipping payment flows (Stripe, PayPal) to conceal proceeds from illegal online sales or knowingly accepting third-party payments without KYC/AML controls.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_sanction: AML Act fine up to CHF 500,000 per missing verification; Penal Code Art. 305bis fine up to CHF 1.5 million with imprisonment up to 5 years.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and anti-money laundering officers are personally prosecutable; asset freezing and confiscation; prohibition from exercising corporate mandates for 5 years; travel ban pending criminal proceedings.
